constraints: Remove a helper only if it is dead in every build configuration, not just absent from the CPU reference build: check the Opencl and Cuda arms before dropping a device-side helper.

The pool lists functions with no caller in the tree (isLinked, fetchStringSettingOrDefault, fetchIntSettingOrDefault, tokenizeByChar, advanceParticleEuler). Confirm each has no reference under any arm, including preprocessor-guarded code, before removing it; drop it from the batch if a guarded caller exists.
Dead-code removal runs first so later passes never transform code that is about to go; do not extract or restructure a function you then delete.
Remove the declaration and the definition together, and any now-unused include that only served it.

divCeil is the only natural candidate: a small free function over (int, int). Templatise it only if every current call still instantiates with the original integer types; add no call that would deduce a narrower or wider type.
Keep AMREX_GPU_HOST_DEVICE / inline qualifiers if present so device callers still compile.

Spread the 14 extractions across the regions: no more than three or four in any one file, and prefer the large repetitive bodies (the border/boundary assignment families, the flux and temperature kernels, the VTK emitters) where a genuine shared helper reads naturally.
Keep expression order and operand types exactly; a helper parameter of a different type inserts a conversion and breaks bit-identity. Suffix literals (1.0 vs 1.0f) stay.

In Cuda/Opencl bodies the helper must carry the same qualifiers (AMREX_GPU_HOST_DEVICE / __device__, inline/AMREX_FORCE_INLINE) and live in a header the kernel already includes; a non-inlined device helper can change FMA contraction, so verify bit-exactness.
Vary the extraction form between sites: a file-static free function, a member helper, a local lambda. Do not apply one template everywhere.

The Cuda functions calculateRsCuda, calculateUvwCuda, calculateTemperatureCuda, calculateFghCuda, calculateDtCuda, setBoundaryValuesCuda, setBoundaryValuesScenarioSpecificCuda and sorSolverCuda are pinned: their signatures must not change, but their bodies may be refactored, so extraction inside them is allowed.
Leave no half-applied extraction: remove the inline copy the helper replaces.
Convert an equality if/else-if ladder to a lookup table only where the table holds exactly the same constants with the same literal types and the control flow is unchanged on every key.

The scenario-specific boundary ladders (assignScenarioBorderValuesCpp, setBorderValuesCaseSpecificMpi, setBoundaryValuesScenarioSpecificCuda, CfdSolverOpencl::setBoundaryValuesScenarioSpecific) are parallel across backends; pick at most one or two so the backends do not all change identically.
In device code use a constexpr array or amrex::GpuArray in the kernel's own scope, never a host global.
setBoundaryValuesScenarioSpecificCuda is pinned: its body may change but its signature may not.
Host code only; device lambdas rarely compile with <numeric>. Avoid the Cuda candidate (arraySumCudaKernel).

Use only order-preserving algorithms (accumulate, transform, for_each, inner_product with sequential semantics). Never std::reduce / transform_reduce or execution policies: they reassociate floating point.
Keep the accumulator type: accumulate(.., 0) gives an int accumulator, so write 0.0 or Real(0) for a floating sum.
Prefer the simple scalar accumulations (parseOptions, tokenizers, NetCdfRecorder::setupRecorder) over the relaxation-sweep reductions, whose loop order the output depends on.
Turn nested ifs into guard clauses only where the control flow is identical on every path; watch for code after the nested block that an early return would skip.

The internal-border assignment families (assignInternalU/V/W/TBorders* across Cpp, Cuda, Mpi) are the richest sites; spread picks across the three backends rather than converting all variants of one border.
Keep guard-clause style consistent with the surrounding file's early-return idiom.
Pinned Cuda functions may have their bodies restructured but not their signatures.
Hoist a loop-invariant subexpression only as the exact same expression with the same type. Never turn a division into a reciprocal multiply: that is a different value.
Hoisting can change FMA contraction; the CPU reference build emits no FMA, but still confirm bit-identity before keeping each instance.

Prefer the long CPU/MPI bodies (computeFghCpp, computeFluxMpi, the relax sweeps, the VTK emitters) where a named invariant reads as a real cleanup. Keep order of floating operations inside reduction loops unchanged.
Do not hoist out of loops that carry a reduction, RNG or I/O in a way that changes their iteration order.
Host code only. Convert manual fopen/fclose to std::ifstream/std::ofstream and new[]/delete[] to std::vector; <fstream> is an allowed standard include to add.
Do not change who allocates GPU, managed or arena memory, and do not change the lifetime of buffers that asynchronous kernels still read.
The IO readers/writers (readPgmImage, loadGeometryData, the VTK and NetCDF recorders, BinaryStream) are the natural sites; vary the replacement (ifstream vs ofstream vs vector) per site.
Keep the exact byte sequence written/read: RAII must not reorder or change the I/O that the oracle parses.
readPgmImage's fixed-size local array is the only candidate. Replace with std::array or std::vector of the same extent; host only.
Keep the buffer contents and read sizes identical.
Guard a memory or range copy only where the guard is true on every valid run or a provable no-op when false (e.g. skip a zero-length memcpy).
Add nothing to the success path and no output; the guard must not change behaviour on any tested input.
Prefer the host buffer copies (BinaryStream, resizeNearest, the PGM scalers, getDataForOutput) over anything inside a kernel.
Add a checked error path to unchecked I/O (fread/fwrite/fopen return values) where the error path is unreachable on valid runs and the success path is unchanged.
No prints and no extra calls on the success path; the oracle parses stdout, so emit nothing new there.
The IO readers/writers and the Opencl file loaders are the natural sites; vary between abort, throw and early-return styles to match each file.
Introduce a parameter object only where every call site is in scope and not frozen; edit every call site in the same instance (call sites cost no CAP but must be listed).
Field types match the parameters' exact types; pass the struct by const& where the parameters were by value or const&.

The very wide host signatures (the initialize family, computeFghCpp, the border setters, the flowline integrator, loadCaseConfigFromFile) are strong candidates; group logically related parameters (grid extents, physical constants, iteration controls) rather than all into one blob.

Do NOT touch the pinned Cuda signatures (calculateRsCuda, calculateUvwCuda, calculateTemperatureCuda, calculateFghCuda, calculateDtCuda, setBoundaryValuesCuda, setBoundaryValuesScenarioSpecificCuda, sorSolverCuda).
A device struct must be trivially copyable and defined in a header the kernel already includes. Keep the composition varied: not every wide function needs the same split.
Respect CAP: the biggest functions appear in several interface groups, so do not stack I1, I2, I3 and I4 all on the same function.
Reorder parameters under one consistent rule per family (inputs, then options, then outputs); update every call site in the same instance.
Arguments must stay free of side effects (evaluation order is unspecified anyway).
Spread across functions that I1 did not already restructure, to keep CAP low per function; prefer the medium-width signatures where a clean inputs/outputs reordering reads naturally.
Do not reorder the pinned Cuda signatures.

Convert output parameters to a returned struct only for outputs the function ALWAYS writes; prefer the candidates with several reference outputs (loadCaseConfigFromFile, relaxSolverOpencl, mpiStartup, parseOptions, computeDtOpencl) over the single-output ones.
Keep the computation order inside the body. In device code return only small trivially copyable structs.
Edit every call site in the instance; avoid the pinned Cuda functions.
Mind CAP interaction with I1/I2 on the same wide functions.
Replace a raw pointer with a typed view of the same element type and extent; never change which memory a kernel reads or writes, or when.
Device candidates are allowed only under the device rules (GpuArray/Array4 views) and must keep the memory space; the pinned Cuda signatures are off limits.
The flux/velocity/border functions carry the most raw pointers; spread picks and vary the view type to match each site.
Update every call site in the instance.
Change a function's home within the SAME file only (free function <-> static member, namespace <-> struct, merge/split a namespace): no file moves, that is the layout stage's job, already done.
Keep AMREX_GPU_HOST_DEVICE and inline qualifiers.
The IO recorders and the solver classes have many members to convert; spread across files and vary the direction (some to free functions, some to static members).
Update every call site; do not touch pinned signatures.
Replace a bool flag parameter with an enum, or split the function into two, only where every call site selects the same branch as before; update all call sites.
The initialize family and the compute-dt / relax variants carry bool flags; prefer an enum where the flag names a mode, a split where it gates a distinct path.
Vary enum-vs-split between sites; avoid pinned signatures.

Regroup struct fields (nest sub-structs, split or merge) only for structs that are NOT serialised, written to output, or mirrored byte-wise to the device; P4's rules apply and every aggregate initialiser and member access must be updated.

The solver context structs (FluidSolverCpp, CfdSolverMpi, FluidSolverCuda, VtkExporter) are candidates, but verify none is copied byte-wise to the device or written to a checkpoint/plotfile before regrouping; skip ByteWriteStream/ByteReadStream if their layout is relied on by serialisation.
This pass runs after the interface passes, so apply it over the final struct shapes, including any struct I1 introduced.
Introduce type aliases only (using/typedef); bulk renaming is the renamer's job. Apply over the final types, including any struct the interface passes introduced.
Alias a frequently used type at a natural boundary (e.g. a solver or recorder type at its public header) and use the alias consistently where it reads naturally; do not alias every type the same way.
Keep the underlying type unchanged; add no behaviour.
